prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE high-fidelity complete screen for HEAV3NS-CODE, a native macOS workspace for the LUMI coding agent. This is a product journey concept, not a website. Flat straight-on screenshot, entire app window fills a 1600x1000 landscape 16:10 image. No perspective, desktop wallpaper, presentation frame, annotations, labels outside the app, or collage.
Shared visual language: a carefully crafted native macOS shell with IDE density and navigation learned from VS Code and Xcode. Neutral graphite window and sidebar (#20242b), deeper code canvas (#171b21), subtly lighter title bar (#282d35), off-white readable text (#edf1f6), secondary text (#b3becd), and restrained blue (#3985f5) for selection and primary actions. Thin separators, natural 6–10px native control corners, SF-style system text and SF Mono-style code. Precise alignment and readable 14–16px body type at this image size. Do not make a generic web dashboard, large marketing headline, bento layout, neon/glass design, or chunky card collage. macOS traffic lights at top left. Product name exact: HEAV3NS-CODE (digit 3). Project name exact: LUMI-NEW.
Every screen uses the same restrained typography, palette, window chrome, and recognizable controls. Short copy is rendered verbatim. These are illustrative prototype states; do not invent factual metrics, prices, model versions, customer claims, account data, or shipped functionality. No invented company logos. Use plain product typography when no logo is provided.
For sign-in states: the app offers Sign in with ChatGPT and hands off to the system browser. Do not paint an in-app password, email, or API-key form or a counterfeit OpenAI login page. Sign-in and AI plan permission are distinct. Show plan-enabled state only in the explicitly described authorized example.
For workspace states: inspection remains read-only and says so. File tabs and syntax tint are visual navigation proposals. No stage, commit, apply, deploy, automatic file deletion, debugger, terminal, or extension-store controls. Show files as a directory hierarchy and classes as an Outline inside the active file, never disguise classes as disk folders.

SCREEN 1: Launch
Splash / launch screen. One complete dark native window with only traffic lights and a small centered title "HEAV3NS-CODE" in the title bar. Center a carefully typeset wordmark "HEAV3NS-CODE", about 36px, and a 16px line "A native workspace for LUMI." Beneath, leave 38px breathing room, then a very small standard progress indicator and text "Preparing your workspace…". A quiet bottom line says "Opening locally". No buttons, sidebar, code, mascot, extra slogan, or illustration. Intentionally calm, beautiful native spacing; no glow or abstract wallpaper. Input reference contributes the dark native material and type only; replace its entire populated workspace with this sparse launch state.

Input image roles: preserve the supplied HEAV3NS-CODE reference's native identity, shared dark material and typography. Where a prior screen is supplied, preserve the app's design system while replacing only the screen content with this scene. Any VS Code image is a navigation reference, never content, branding or annotations to copy.
